headline_marked: 5 bullets found in body as [[journalist shot dead in Netrokona]]
headline: 5 bullets found in body as journalist shot dead in Netrokona
summary: Lutfuzzaman Alif, a representative for Ruposhi Bangla and operator of a Facebook page, was killed by gunmen in Durgapur.
details: Lutfuzzaman Alif, a journalist for private television channel Ruposhi Bangla and operator of the 'Detective Article' Facebook page, was shot dead by gunmen in Durgapur, Netrokona.
The incident occurred around 8:15 PM on Thursday at Utrail Bazar on the Shyamganj-Birishiri road. Witnesses say two youths on a motorcycle fired multiple shots at Alif while he was sitting at a shop.
Local residents rushed to help, causing the attackers to flee. Alif was taken to the Upazila Health Complex but died shortly after.
Durgapur Police Station OC Khandakar Shaker Ahmed Khan stated that five bullets were found in the victim's head, neck, and chest. Police are currently conducting raids to arrest the suspects.
Alif, a resident of Kolmakanda, lived with his in-laws in the Birishiri area. Netrokona Superintendent of Police Md. Tariqul Islam visited the scene following the incident.
This is not the first attack on the journalist; on November 10, he was hacked and injured by miscreants at Teribazar Ghat. He frequently wrote about drug smuggling on social media.
caption:
Five bullets to the head, neck, and chest. A journalist in Netrokona has been shot dead by gunmen.

Lutfuzzaman Alif, a journalist for private television channel Ruposhi Bangla and operator of the 'Detective Article' Facebook page, was shot dead by gunmen in Durgapur, Netrokona.

The incident occurred around 8:15 PM on Thursday at Utrail Bazar on the Shyamganj-Birishiri road. Witnesses say two youths on a motorcycle fired multiple shots at Alif while he was sitting at a shop.

Local residents rushed to help, causing the attackers to flee. Alif was taken to the Upazila Health Complex but died shortly after.

Durgapur Police Station OC Khandakar Shaker Ahmed Khan stated that five bullets were found in the victim's head, neck, and chest. Police are currently conducting raids to arrest the suspects.

Alif, a resident of Kolmakanda, lived with his in-laws in the Birishiri area. Netrokona Superintendent of Police Md. Tariqul Islam visited the scene following the incident.

This is not the first attack on the journalist; on November 10, he was hacked and injured by miscreants at Teribazar Ghat. He frequently wrote about drug smuggling on social media.

#Bangladesh #Netrokona #Journalism #CrimeNews #PressFreedom

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: [[Youth beaten to death]] in Satkhira after Facebook live incites crowd
headline: Youth beaten to death in Satkhira after Facebook live incites crowd
summary: A man accused of blasphemy was beaten to death in Satkhira after a Facebook live session gathered a mob. He was assaulted multiple times, even after being taken to the hospital.
details: Wahiduzzaman Shamim, 38, was beaten to death in Debhata, Satkhira, on Tuesday. The incident occurred after an audio clip of his conversation, allegedly containing blasphemous remarks, was spread on Facebook. A local, Fazlul Haque, allegedly used Facebook Live twice to gather people, first to play the audio and then to incite a crowd at a local doctor's chamber where Shamim was receiving treatment.

During the live sessions, Fazlul Haque allegedly shared Shamim's address and urged people to gather. Hundreds of people reportedly assembled, and pressure was applied to hand Shamim over to them. Videos show Shamim being beaten on the ground, with people stepping on his chest. Another video shows a procession demanding punishment for Shamim.

Shamim's younger brother, Tausif Rahman, stated that Shamim had been suffering from mental health issues and his erratic behavior was known to the community. He alleged that a group, identified as supporters of Jamaat, led by Fazlul Haque, beat his brother to death. Shamim, an alumnus of Jagannath University and a Kamil graduate, is survived by his wife and two sons.

Shamim's elder brother, Abdul Jalil, explained that an audio clip of a quarrel between Shamim and his wife was spread on Monday, leading to accusations of blasphemy. This triggered an attack on their home, with attempts to break down the door and walls. The family claims Shamim was first assaulted at the Subarnabad market, then returned home and attempted suicide by consuming poison before being taken to a local doctor.

Police rescued Shamim and admitted him to the Debhata Upazila Health Complex. However, according to Dr. Md. Saiful Islam, over a hundred people stormed the hospital, assaulted Shamim again, and dragged him outside to continue the beating. Shamim died on the way to Satkhira Medical College Hospital.

Fazlul Haque, when contacted, acknowledged that taking the law into one's own hands is a crime but stated that the religious law differs for those who insult the Prophet. He claimed to have led protests in the past for similar issues. Haque, a former mosque imam, now works as a butcher and a motorcycle taxi driver.

Debhata Upazila Jamaat Secretary Imdadul Haque condemned the killing, stating that anyone with a complaint should be handed over to the law. He clarified that the incident should not be portrayed as a party activity of Jamaat-Shibir and that the party does not support such violence.
